findings.text: Plans 1 to 4 are built on main. Plan 3 built only the rules, `cruise diagnose` and `cruise audit`. `tidy`, `package`, `inventory` and `profile` are follow-ups, so nothing in the repo writes a package from source files yet, apart from the sample package's own build script.

The one dataset 'already converted by hand' has to be converted again. The hand-made Ozone package was built on a draft of the format, and the contract rejects it: `cruise diagnose` stops at structure.manifest-invalid with 8 validation errors, the first being version '1.0.0'.

findings.text: All six FEMC records share one non-standard shape, so one set of rules covers them all. The title, description, purpose and coverage sit on the dataTable. People sit under role-named elements. Attributes use measurementType. The distribution tag is misspelled distibution. Only the aerial survey has code lists, written as enumeratedDomain directly on the attribute.

The core importer leaves one archive's non-standard EML to that archive's converter, in its own words: 'Tolerating one archive's non-standard EML is left to that archive's converter.' The handoff says FEMC is one config file plus the ecology profile, and that nothing in the core may be specific to FEMC.

The records and the files disagree in 3 of 5 tables. FIA has 49 columns that aren't described. Data Rescue describes 25 columns the file doesn't have. The aerial survey describes 27 of 42 columns, and three names only match after a change of case or the shapefile's 10-character limit. A converter that takes the column list from the file and matches descriptions onto it handles all three.
No FEMC record states rights in EML. Rights come only from the license FEMC's web page shows, which SOURCES.md records: four show 'Linked - third party determines data license' and two show none.

rounds.take:
**What Plan 5 has to build is bigger than the brief assumed, in one way, and smaller in another.**

Bigger: the brief says one dataset is converted and five remain. In fact none are: the hand-made Ozone package uses a draft of the format and the contract rejects it outright. Nothing in the repo writes a package from source files either, since Plan 3 left `cruise package` for later. So all six need converting, and something has to do the converting.

Smaller: FEMC's six EML records all share the same non-standard shape (findings above). One set of rules for reading that shape covers every record, rather than six one-off scripts.

So the fork is **what does the converting, and where does it live?** I see three ways:

- **A FEMC converter beside FEMC's config, outside the core** (my recommendation). One small committed module, kept with FEMC's archive config file. It takes a downloaded dataset folder (the `eml.xml` plus the download) and writes a package. It reshapes FEMC's EML into what the standard `from_eml` reads and lets `from_eml` do the rest. It takes the column list from the actual file, matches the record's descriptions onto those columns, and writes down everything it could not import. Rights come from what `SOURCES.md` records for each page. It runs on all six, then `cruise audit` over the folder gives the numbers for the FEMC report (Plan 10b). The contract and cruise stay unchanged.
- **Teach the core importer FEMC's quirks.** Fewer files, but it breaks the generic-first rule and the importer's own stated design.
- **Paper only.** Fix the corpus list, the order and the expected problems, and build nothing. This is the handoff's literal 'Done when', but the report would then have no audit numbers to cite.

Growing the corpus to 10 to 20 datasets and approaching the FEMC contact come after this, as their own decisions, once the converter has run on the six.

calls.name: Converter location
calls.question: Where does the FEMC converter live?
calls.took: `examples/femc/`: FEMC's `archive.yaml` and a small uv workspace package `femc` (src layout, its own tests), so ruff, mypy and pytest in `just check` cover it. It depends on archive-contract only.
calls.instead: A plain script beside the config, outside CI, like the sample package's `_build/make.py`.
calls.why: The handoff makes FEMC 'one config file plus the ecology profile' and the first reference deployment; keeping the converter with that config keeps the core generic, and a workspace member gets the same checks as the rest of the code.

calls.name: Read FEMC through from_eml
calls.question: How does the converter read FEMC's EML?
calls.took: It rewrites FEMC's shape into standard EML (title and description up from the dataTable, entityName from the table, role-named personnel to individualName plus role, measurementType to measurementScale, distibution to distribution, enumeratedDomain into its scale) and passes the result to the unchanged `from_eml`.
calls.instead: A separate FEMC reader that builds the manifest itself.
calls.why: from_eml already maps every standard element to the manifest and lists what it skips; one rewrite step reuses all of it, and any later core improvement reaches FEMC too.

calls.name: Columns from the file
calls.question: Whose column list wins when the EML and the file disagree?
calls.took: The file's. Each real column becomes a field; an EML attribute is matched to it by exact name, then case-insensitively, then by the shapefile's 10-character truncation, and the EML's spelling goes in `archive:sourceName`. Described columns not in the file are listed as not imported.
calls.instead: Keep the EML's list and flag the mismatch, so fields can describe columns that don't exist.
calls.why: A package describes the data it holds; this handles FIA's 49 undescribed columns, Data Rescue's 25 extra attributes and the aerial survey's three renamed ones with one rule, and needs no change to the core validator's case-sensitive check.

calls.name: Rights from SOURCES.md
calls.question: Where do rights come from, since no FEMC record states them?
calls.took: From the license each dataset page shows, as recorded in SOURCES.md: a Creative Commons license becomes a license, 'Linked - third party determines data license' becomes `third-party` with FEMC's words as the statement, and no license shown becomes `undetermined`.
calls.instead: Leave every package `undetermined` until someone checks each page.
calls.why: The page is FEMC's own statement, recorded at download; the audit then shows the third-party packages lack a named licensor, which is a real finding for the report.

calls.name: Conversion order
calls.question: In what order are the datasets converted?
calls.took: 1 Ozone (small, the baseline). 2 Data Rescue (EML lists columns the file lacks, personal columns, short description). 3 IMPROVE (239 columns, day-first dates, value/uncertainty/flag groups). 4 Camels Hump (linked, URL only in the citation). 5 Aerial survey (shapefile set, code lists, attribute table, renamed columns). 6 FIA (155 MB, 49 undescribed columns). Then the additions DCSN1 settles.
calls.instead: Convert the hardest first (aerial survey), so its problems shape the converter early.
calls.why: Each step adds one new problem to a converter that already handles the earlier ones, which is the brief's 'in order of what each will teach us'.

calls.name: Themes in the config
calls.question: What goes in FEMC's archive config, given packages have no theme field?
calls.took: publisher, profiles [core, ecology] and FEMC's six themes as its own project listing names them (air, climate change, forest, soil, water, wildlife). Access is set per dataset on each package (`archive:access`), since FEMC sets it per dataset, not per theme. A per-package theme field is Plan 2's follow-up (its PARK5, archive:themes checked against the config's themes); when it lands, the converter can fill it.
calls.instead: Add a theme field to the manifest now.
calls.why: The handoff says seven themes, but FEMC's own listing uses six top-level themes across its 581 projects; and the theme field belongs to the contract, which Plan 2 owns and has recorded as a follow-up.

calls.name: Gaps stay gaps
calls.question: What does the converter do with a gap in FEMC's record?
calls.took: Writes what the record says and nothing more: a 21-character description stays, coverage keeps the record's dates (with `end: unknown` where only a start is given), and the citation goes in `archive:citation`. cruise reports the gaps.
calls.instead: Fill gaps from the citation, the file name or the project text.
calls.why: The handoff's rule: nothing is invented about FEMC. The gaps are the evidence the report needs.

calls.name: Files and the not-imported list
calls.question: Which files go where in each converted package, and where is the not-imported list kept?
calls.took: Downloaded files go under data/ as downloaded (the aerial survey's zip unpacked, nothing else changed, since tidying is Plan 3's later work). FEMC's eml.xml goes under original/ as a file resource, so the source record travels with the package. The zip itself isn't copied again, since every member sits unchanged in data/ and SOURCES.md checksums the zip. The not-imported list goes in the package's _build/not-imported.txt, which the contract treats as outside the package content.
calls.instead: Keep a full untouched copy of each download under original/ as well (155 MB more for FIA), and put the not-imported list in docs/ so it is archived with the package.
calls.why: No cleaning happens in this plan, so a second byte-identical copy adds size and nothing else; the not-imported list is a converter report for us and the FEMC report, not part of the dataset.

calls.name: Audit counts only in public
calls.question: What of the audit output is committed to this public planning folder?
calls.took: Only counts with no evidence values: per dataset its errors, warnings, notes, completeness score and the rule ids that fired. The full diagnose and audit output stays under practice-data/audit/, which is git-ignored.
calls.instead: Commit the full output, evidence values included, to documents/; that publishes data values from datasets with no license or a third-party one.
calls.why: Findings quote up to 20 data values each, and the repo is public; 'nothing from practice-data is committed' exists to keep those private. The coordinating session raised it in its scope check of the spec.

approved.body:
# FEMC migration and practice corpus

## Goal

A converter that turns a dataset downloaded from FEMC's public archive (its EML record plus its download) into a package the contract accepts. It runs on a practice corpus of ten FEMC datasets, and `cruise audit` over the result gives the FEMC report (Plan 10b) its counts. FEMC's quirks are handled beside FEMC's own config, so `archive_contract` and `cruise` stay unchanged and generic.

## The converter

The converter lives in `examples/femc/`, beside FEMC's `archive.yaml`, as a small uv workspace package named `femc` with a `src/` layout and its own tests. It depends on `archive-contract` only, and `just check` covers it with ruff, mypy and pytest like every other package.

It takes one dataset folder from `practice-data/femc/<dataset>/` (the `eml.xml`, the download if there is one, and that dataset's row of `SOURCES.md`) and writes one package folder under `practice-data/packages/<dataset>/`. It is run as `uv run femc convert <dataset-folder> <out-folder>`. It writes the manifest, `checksums.sha256` and the generated `README.md` with the contract's own functions, and nothing in `practice-data/` is committed.

Rests on: AGNT1, AGNT8

## Reading FEMC's EML

All FEMC records share one non-standard shape, so the converter reads them in two steps. First it rewrites the record into standard EML:

- the `dataTable`'s `title`, `description`, `purpose` and `coverage` move up to the dataset, and the table gets an `entityName`;
- role-named personnel (`principalInvestigator`, `contentProvider`) become `individualName` plus `role`;
- `publisher`'s inner `metadataProvider` becomes the publisher party itself;
- `measurementType` becomes `measurementScale`, and an `enumeratedDomain` sitting directly on an attribute moves into its scale;
- the misspelled `distibution` becomes `distribution`;
- a coverage with only a begin date gets `end: unknown`.

Then it passes the rewritten record to the unchanged `from_eml`, which maps every standard element to the manifest, project and code lists. FEMC's preferred citation goes in `archive:citation`. For a linked record, the data's URL is taken from the citation's "Available online at:" text, the only place FEMC records it. Anything neither step reads goes on the package's not-imported list.

The converter writes what the record says and nothing more. A description shorter than the core 50 characters stays as it is; coverage keeps the record's dates even where the file name disagrees; a record with no creator gets none. The audit reports each gap.

Rests on: AGNT2, AGNT7

## Columns and files

The file is the truth about its columns. Each real column becomes a field, typed from the file. An EML attribute is matched to a column by exact name, then without regard to case, then by the shapefile's 10-character truncation; the EML's spelling, when it differs, goes in `archive:sourceName`. An attribute with no column is listed as not imported, and a column with no attribute gets a field with no description. The core validator's case-sensitive check is left as it is, since field names are written exactly as the file spells them.

Downloaded files go under `data/` as downloaded, with nothing changed: tidying is Plan 3's later work. A zip is unpacked and not copied again; the aerial survey's shapefile parts become one `vector` resource with `archive:files` and an `archive:attributes` schema naming its `.dbf` columns as the `.dbf` spells them; its CSV (the attribute table without geometry) becomes its own `table` resource, and its XLSX an alternate of the CSV. FEMC's `eml.xml` goes under `original/` as a `file` resource. The not-imported list, one line per element or attribute with the reason, goes in the package's `_build/not-imported.txt`, which the contract treats as outside the package content.

Rests on: AGNT3, AGNT8

## Rights and access

No FEMC record states rights, so rights come from the license each dataset page shows, as recorded in `SOURCES.md` at download:

- a Creative Commons license becomes a license with its SPDX id;
- "Linked - third party determines data license" becomes `archive:rightsStatus: third-party`, with FEMC's words as the statement;
- no license shown becomes `undetermined`, so the package can be audited but not published.

Access follows FEMC's own label for the dataset: Downloadable is `open`, By request is `by-request`, Description only is `description-only`. A linked record is `open`, with a `linked` resource.

Rests on: AGNT4

## The corpus and its order

Ten datasets, converted in this order, each adding one problem the converter has not met yet:

| # | Dataset | What it teaches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Ozone Bioindicators | The baseline: a small table. Converted again, since the hand-made package uses a draft format the contract rejects. |
| 2 | Data Rescue Inventory | The record describes 25 columns the file lacks; personal columns; a 21-character description. |
| 3 | IMPROVE fine aerosol | 239 columns, day-first dates, value, uncertainty, detection limit and flag per analyte. |
| 4 | Camels Hump census_data | A linked record whose URL is only in the citation. |
| 5 | Aerial detection survey | A shapefile set, code lists on attributes, an attribute table, renamed columns. |
| 6 | FIA tree-level | 155 MB and 49 undescribed columns. |
| 7 | Vegetation Class Raster | A raster, licensed CC0. |
| 8 | Mount Mansfield Quadrat Images | Photographs, licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. |
| 9 | Development Related Projects with Threatened or Endangered Species | By request, ongoing, protected species: metadata only. |
| 10 | 1991 White clover clones as a biomonitor | Description only: metadata only. |

Datasets 7 to 10 are new. Their EML records are saved from each page's `/eml_xmlview`; datasets 7 and 8 are downloaded by hand through FEMC's public pages; each gets a row in `SOURCES.md` with the license its page shows and a line in `CHECKSUMS.sha256`. The raster and image files' exact formats are read when they are downloaded, and they map to the contract's existing `raster` and `media` kinds.

Rests on: DCSN1, AGNT5

## FEMC's archive config

`examples/femc/archive.yaml` holds FEMC's config: the publisher (the Forest Ecosystem Monitoring Cooperative), the profiles `core` and `ecology`, and FEMC's six themes as its own project listing names them: air, climate change, forest, soil, water and wildlife. Access is set per package, not per theme. A per-package theme field is Plan 2's follow-up (its PARK5); the converter fills it once it exists.

Rests on: AGNT6

## The audit

Once the ten are converted, `cruise diagnose` runs on each and `cruise audit` over `practice-data/packages/`. Their full output, whose evidence quotes data values, stays under `practice-data/audit/`, which is not committed. This folder's `documents/` gets only the counts the FEMC report needs, with no evidence values: per dataset its errors, warnings, notes, completeness score and the rule ids that fired. Plan 5 makes no contact with FEMC and drafts no request to them: the contact and any bulk-export ask belong to Plan 10b, which takes the audit numbers from here.

Rests on: DCSN2, AGNT9

## Risk and cost

Risk: low. The converter writes only new package folders under `practice-data/packages/` on Court's machine and adds new code under `examples/femc/`; nothing in the core changes and nothing is deployed. A wrong conversion is undone by deleting the package folder and running the converter again. The one thing that must not happen is committing FEMC's data, since `practice-data/` is git-ignored and licenses vary.

Cost: two downloads by hand from Court (the raster and the images). No new programs: the converter uses the contract and the standard library.

Rests on: DCSN1, AGNT1

## Left out

- Contacting FEMC, and the bulk-export request: Plan 10b.
- Tidying the data (renaming columns, fixing values, writing `changes.jsonl` steps): `cruise tidy`, a Plan 3 follow-up.
- A generic `cruise package` command: a Plan 3 follow-up. The FEMC converter is not its first draft.
- A per-package theme field (Plan 2's PARK5) and taxonomic coverage (Plan 2's PARK6).
- Code lists published outside a record, such as the FIA database manual's codes: those columns stay `undocumented`.
- Growing the corpus past ten, and any scrape of FEMC's archive.
- Uploading the packages to an archive: Plan 7.

Rests on: DCSN2, AGNT7

## How we'll know it works

- Each of the ten packages passes `cruise diagnose` with no structure error. Quality findings are expected; they are the point.
- Every package's `_build/not-imported.txt` accounts for each element and attribute the converter did not map, so nothing is dropped silently.
- The converter's tests, on invented records written in FEMC's shape (none of FEMC's own records are committed), cover each rewrite and the column matching, and `just check` exits 0.
- `cruise audit` over the ten runs to the end; its full output is under `practice-data/audit/`, and the counts with no evidence values are in this folder's `documents/`.

Rests on: AGNT3, AGNT8, AGNT9

approved.body:
# PLAN1: The FEMC converter and the ten-dataset corpus

## Spec

`spec.md` in this folder, approved. This plan builds all of it: the `femc` package in `examples/femc/` with FEMC's `archive.yaml`, the ten conversions, and the audit counts.

## The change

A new uv workspace member, `examples/femc/`, holding:

- `archive.yaml`: FEMC's archive config.
- `src/femc/eml.py`: `standardize(xml: str) -> tuple[str, list[str]]`, which rewrites a FEMC record into standard EML and returns the lines of what it dropped.
- `src/femc/convert.py`: `convert(dataset: Path, sources: Path, out: Path) -> Path`, which writes one package from one `practice-data/femc/<dataset>/` folder and its row of `SOURCES.md`.
- `src/femc/cli.py`: `femc convert <dataset-folder> <out-folder>`, with `--sources` defaulting to the `SOURCES.md` beside the dataset folder.
- `tests/`, with invented records and files written in FEMC's shape. None of FEMC's own records or files are committed.

The root `pyproject.toml` gains the member, its `src` on `mypy_path`, `examples/femc` in pytest's `testpaths` and `femc` in isort's first-party list, so `just check` covers it. `archive_contract` and `cruise` are not changed.

The ten datasets are already on Court's machine: the four new ones were fetched on 2026-11-13 through FEMC's public pages (two downloads through the anonymous Download Data form, four EML records from `/eml_xmlview`), with rows in `SOURCES.md` and lines in `CHECKSUMS.sha256` (`shasum -a 256 -c` passes for every file). Facts found while fetching them that the converter must handle:

- Three of the four new records name their project `researchProject`, not `project`.
- Vegetation Class Raster is an ESRI ArcInfo binary grid: a zip of nine `.adf` and companion files that only work together.
- Mount Mansfield Quadrat Images is a zip of 88 JPEG photographs, 209 MB.
- The `dataTable`'s `shortName` holds the download's file name in some records and is empty in others.

## Left out

Everything in the spec's Left out, and:

- Any change to `archive_contract` or `cruise`. If a conversion shows the core can't hold something FEMC has, it goes to the coordinating session as a note for Plan 2, not into this plan.
- Reading the raster's cells or the photographs' contents: they are recorded as files with sizes and hashes, nothing more.
- A command that converts a whole folder at once: the ten are run one by one.

## Where

- Code: `examples/femc/` on a branch from `origin/main` in a worktree at `.worktrees/research-archive-in-a-box/plan5/femc-converter`, merged by pull request.
- Inputs: `practice-data/femc/` in the main clone, read only.
- Outputs: `practice-data/packages/<dataset>/` and `practice-data/audit/` in the main clone, git-ignored. The hand-made `practice-data/packages/ozone-bioindicators/` is replaced by the converted one, after moving the old folder to `practice-data/packages/_draft-ozone-bioindicators/` so nothing is lost.
- Counts for the FEMC report: `documents/femc-audit-counts.md` in this planning folder.

### Task 1: The femc package and FEMC's config

**Does:** Creates the `examples/femc/` workspace member with an empty `femc` package, its `femc` command (printing help), `py.typed`, and FEMC's `archive.yaml`; wires it into the root `pyproject.toml`; adds one test that `archive.yaml` loads with `archive_contract.config.load_config`.
**Files:** `examples/femc/pyproject.toml`, `examples/femc/archive.yaml`, `examples/femc/src/femc/__init__.py`, `examples/femc/src/femc/cli.py`, `examples/femc/src/femc/py.typed`, `examples/femc/tests/test_config.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`
**Checks:** `just check-python`; `uv run femc --help`
**Serves:** none (rests on calls AGNT1, AGNT6)

`archive.yaml`: `publisher: Forest Ecosystem Monitoring Cooperative`, `profiles: [core, ecology]`, `themes: [air, climate change, forest, soil, water, wildlife]`. No `infrastructure` section: FEMC is not deployed by this plan. The package depends on `archive-contract` only (workspace source).

### Task 2: Reading FEMC's EML

**Does:** Writes `femc.eml.standardize`, which rewrites a FEMC record into standard EML so the unchanged `from_eml` reads it, and returns what it dropped.
**Files:** `examples/femc/src/femc/eml.py`, `examples/femc/tests/test_eml.py`, `examples/femc/tests/fixtures/eml/*.xml`
**Checks:** `just check-python`
**Serves:** none (rests on calls AGNT2, AGNT7)

The rewrites, each with a test on an invented record:

- `researchProject` becomes `project`.
- The `dataTable`'s `title`, `description` (as `abstract/para`), `purpose` (as `purpose/para`) and `coverage` move up to the dataset; the table gets `entityName` from its title and `entityDescription` from its description. An empty `purpose` or `shortName` is dropped silently; the `dataTable`'s non-empty `shortName` is dropped and reported.
- Project `personnel` children named for a role (`principalInvestigator`, `contentProvider`, any other) become `personnel` elements with `individualName` (`givenName`, `surName`) and `role` set to the element's name. An empty `personnel` is removed.
- `publisher/metadataProvider`'s children move up into `publisher`.
- `measurementType` becomes `measurementScale`; an `enumeratedDomain` directly on an attribute moves into its scale's `nonNumericDomain`; an empty scale element is left for `from_eml` to report.
- `distibution` becomes `distribution`.
- A `rangeOfDates` with a `beginDate` and no `endDate` gets the end marker the EML export writes for `end: unknown` (`archive_contract.exports.eml.END_UNKNOWN`), so `from_eml` reads it back as unknown.
- `physical/citation` is removed from the record and returned separately, for `archive:citation`.

The test for the whole: `from_eml(standardize(record))` on an invented record in FEMC's full shape gives a title, a description, a temporal coverage, a project with its people, one resource with its fields, and the code list, and every line `from_eml` skips is in the returned list.

### Task 3: Writing a package

**Does:** Writes `femc.convert.convert` and the `femc convert` command: reads the record through `standardize` and `from_eml`, lays out the files, matches columns, sets rights and access, and writes the manifest, `checksums.sha256`, `README.md` and `_build/not-imported.txt`.
**Files:** `examples/femc/src/femc/convert.py`, `examples/femc/src/femc/cli.py`, `examples/femc/tests/test_convert.py`, `examples/femc/tests/fixtures/datasets/**`
**Checks:** `just check-python`
**Serves:** DCSN1 (rests on calls AGNT3, AGNT4, AGNT7, AGNT8)

What it writes:

- **Identity.** `name` and `id` are the dataset folder's name; `version` is `"1"`; `archive:legacyIdentifiers` holds the EML package id (from `from_eml`) and FEMC's object name (`femc-object`, such as `VMC.23.214`); `homepage` is the source page from `SOURCES.md`; `archive:citation` is the record's citation.
- **Rights and access** from the `SOURCES.md` row: "CC0 - Public domain" becomes license `CC0-1.0`, "CC BY-NC-SA 4.0" becomes `CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0` (the only two the corpus shows; any other text stops the conversion with a clear message), "Linked - third party determines data license" becomes `third-party` with those words as the statement, "None shown on the overview page" becomes `undetermined`. Access: a "none (By request)" data file is `by-request`, "none (Description only)" is `description-only`, everything else `open`.
- **Files.** A CSV goes to `data/` unchanged as a `table`. A zip is unpacked into `data/<zip stem>/` and not copied: a shapefile set becomes one `vector` resource with `archive:files` (every part, `.shp.xml`, `.sbn` and `.sbx` included) and `archive:attributes` naming the `.dbf` columns as the `.dbf` header spells them; a CSV beside it becomes its own `table`, and an `.xlsx` of the same name an alternate of that CSV; an ArcInfo grid (a folder or zip holding `hdr.adf`) becomes one `raster` resource with `archive:files` for every file; each JPEG becomes its own `media` resource named from its file stem. `eml.xml` goes to `original/eml.xml` as a `file` resource. Every file gets `bytes` and a `sha256` hash.
- **Columns.** For a table, the columns are read from the file's header row; each becomes a field. The record's attributes are matched to columns by exact name, then case-insensitively, then by a 10-character truncation for a shapefile's columns; a match carries the attribute's description, its declared type and its code list, and the attribute's name goes in `archive:sourceName` when it differs. Where the record declares no type, the type is inferred from the column's values (integer, number, date, otherwise string) with the standard library, and the inference is listed. Attributes with no column, and columns with no attribute, are listed.
- **Linked records.** When there is no data file and the citation contains "Available online at:" followed by a URL, a `linked` resource points at that URL with no format.
- **The not-imported list**, `_build/not-imported.txt`: the lines `standardize` dropped, the lines `from_eml` skipped, attributes with no column, columns with no attribute, and inferred types, one per line, each with its reason.
- `checksums.sha256` and `README.md` are written with `archive_contract.validate.package_files` and `archive_contract.exports.readme.render_readme`, as the sample package's build does.

Tests run `convert` on invented dataset folders, each a few rows: a CSV table whose record describes one extra attribute and misses one column and uses a different case for another; a linked record with the URL only in its citation; a zip holding a three-feature shapefile set with a CSV and an `.xlsx` (written in the test with `pyshp` and `openpyxl`, already dev dependencies); a metadata-only By-request record. Each test asserts the manifest's resources, fields and rights, that `archive_contract.validate.validate_package` returns no findings, and the exact lines of `_build/not-imported.txt`.

### Task 4: Convert the ten

**Does:** Runs `femc convert` on each of the ten datasets in the spec's order and `cruise diagnose` on each result, fixing the converter until no package has a structure error. Every fix that a real dataset forces gets a test on an invented record or file showing the same case.
**Files:** `examples/femc/src/femc/*.py` and `examples/femc/tests/**` for fixes; outputs under `practice-data/packages/` (not committed)
**Checks:** `just check-python`; for each dataset, `uv run femc convert ../../../research-archive-in-a-box/practice-data/femc/<dataset> <out>` exits 0, then `uv run cruise diagnose <package> --json | jq -e '[.findings[] | select(.ruleId | startswith("structure."))] | length == 0'` exits 0
**Serves:** DCSN1 (rests on call AGNT5)

The order: ozone-bioindicators, data-rescue-inventory, improve-fine-aerosol, camels-hump-census, aerial-detection-survey, fia-tree-level, vegetation-class-raster, mount-mansfield-quadrat-images, development-related-te-species, white-clover-biomonitor. Before the first run, move the hand-made `practice-data/packages/ozone-bioindicators/` to `practice-data/packages/_draft-ozone-bioindicators/`. A blocking quality error (a missing creator, an undetermined license) is expected and is not a failure: only `structure.*` findings fail this check. If a dataset needs something the core can't hold, stop and bring it to Court with the evidence rather than working around it.

### Task 5: The audit and its counts

**Does:** Runs `cruise audit` over the ten with FEMC's config, keeps the full output under `practice-data/audit/`, and writes the counts the FEMC report needs, with no evidence values, to this folder's `documents/femc-audit-counts.md`.
**Files:** `docs/specs/2026-11-13-femc-migration-and-practice-corpus/documents/femc-audit-counts.md`; `practice-data/audit/audit.json` and `practice-data/audit/<dataset>.json` (not committed)
**Checks:** `uv run cruise audit --config examples/femc/archive.yaml --json <packages-folder> > <audit>/audit.json` exits 0; `jq -e '.packages | length == 10' <audit>/audit.json` exits 0
**Serves:** DCSN2 (rests on call AGNT9)

`femc-audit-counts.md` has one table row per dataset: its name, errors, warnings, notes, completeness score, and the find, understand and trust counts; then, per dataset, the rule ids that fired with how many times each. It is built from `audit.json` with `jq` and holds no `evidence`, `values` or `message` text, since messages can quote data. Its header says which commit of the converter and of cruise produced it and when. It is committed with the planning folder's next commit.

messages.text: From Plan 2 (package format and contract), built and merged on main in schuettc/research-in-a-box. Read docs/specs/2026-11-12-generic-package-format-and-contract/documents/femc-paper-test.md first: it writes FEMC's six practice datasets in the format and lists, per record, what the standard EML importer (archive_contract.imports.eml.from_eml) reads and skips. FEMC's EML is almost entirely non-standard (title, description and coverage on the dataTable; role-named personnel; measurementType; the misspelled distibution), so from_eml reads only the package id, the project and some parties. Tolerating those quirks is yours. Two notes: the validator matches a shapefile's described columns to the .dbf case-sensitively, and FEMC names may need a case-insensitive match; the eight gaps the paper test found are now fields in the format.

From the coordinating session for research-in-a-box. Court asked that every planning session know this. Muster alias: personal-personal/generic-package-format-and-contract (the name is left over from Plan 2; this session now coordinates all the plans).

1. Send cross-plan questions here first: anything that touches another plan's interface, ownership or order, or the overall direction. Ask over muster or with diazo_note to this alias. Questions only Court can answer still go on your own page as decision cards.
2. Send a one-line muster message here when your understanding is confirmed, your spec is printed, each plan is printed, and the build is done. I check each spec and plan for scope before Court approves it.
3. Record anything other plans rely on in the Decision log of docs/planning-handoff.md.
4. Keep it small. Plans 1 and 2 are built: the repo, the uv and npm workspaces, archive_contract, the exports and the sample package. Build on them and don't rebuild. Plan only what your brief needs to work end to end now, and put everything else in follow-ups. Size checks to the risk. Question every option, config field and fallback that no real case needs yet.
5. FEMC is the test afterwards, never the source of the design (Plan 2's PRIN1).

From Plan 2 (package format and contract): the per-package theme field is now a follow-up on Plan 2 itself (PARK5, archive:themes checked against the config's themes), since the contract is Plan 2's; Plan 6 raised the same gap, along with taxonomic coverage (PARK6). So you needn't record one for Plans 6 and 8. Keeping themes in FEMC's config only is right for now.
